blogs.title: When Diabetes Isn’t Type 1 or Type 2: Spotting HNF1A‑MODY in the Clinic
blogs.description: A step‑by‑step review of the clinical clues that should raise suspicion for MODY—early‑onset hyperglycaemia, strong autosomal‑dominant family history, negative autoantibodies, low‑grade insulin resistance, and glycosuria. We will walk readers through practical bedside algorithms (including the Exeter MODY calculator), their limitations in non‑European populations, and how to decide when to order genetic testing.

blogs.title: Precision Therapy for HNF1A‑MODY: From Sulfonylureas to GLP‑1 Agonists
blogs.description: An evidence‑based discussion of pharmacologic options for HNF1A‑MODY, comparing low‑dose sulfonylureas, GLP‑1 receptor agonists, DPP‑4 inhibitors, and the pitfalls of SGLT‑2 inhibitors in this setting. The post will use the presented case to illustrate how a GLP‑1 agonist can replace insulin and preserve β‑cell function, and will provide a treatment decision tree for clinicians encountering a newly diagnosed MODY patient.

blogs.title: The Genetics Frontier: Interpreting Novel HNF1A Variants Using ACMG Guidelines
blogs.description: A deep dive into variant interpretation for monogenic diabetes. We’ll explain the ACMG criteria, illustrate how the p.N270S (c.809A>G) mutation was classified as pathogenic, and discuss tools such as AlphaMissense, segregation analysis, and functional domain mapping. The article will also cover the growing role of next‑generation sequencing panels and how to handle variants of uncertain significance in everyday practice.

blogs.title: Beyond the Calculator: Challenges of MODY Screening in Asian and Multiracial Populations
blogs.description: Explores why existing MODY probability tools (derived from predominantly White European cohorts) may misestimate risk in Asian, Hispanic, and mixed‑ethnicity patients. We’ll review epidemiologic data from China, Denmark, and Russia, discuss the impact of rising obesity on phenotype overlap, and propose practical adjustments for clinicians working in diverse settings.

blogs.title: Small‑Fiber Autonomic Dysfunction in Early HNF1A‑MODY: A Forgotten Clinical Sign?
blogs.description: Analyzes the unexpected finding of severe sudomotor impairment in the case report, linking it to autonomic neuropathy in early‑stage MODY. The blog will summarize current evidence on autonomic testing (Sudoscan, heart‑rate variability) in monogenic diabetes, discuss pathophysiologic mechanisms, and suggest when to incorporate autonomic screening into MODY work‑ups.

blogs.title: Cost‑Effectiveness of Universal vs. Targeted Genetic Testing for Young‑Onset Diabetes
blogs.description: A health‑economics focused piece that models the downstream savings of correctly diagnosing MODY (avoiding unnecessary insulin, reducing hypoglycaemia, preventing complications) versus the upfront costs of NGS panels. The case’s rapid HbA1c improvement and medication simplification will serve as a real‑world example to illustrate potential budget impact for health systems.
